title: Incidents: Stopping, Reporting & First Aid
whatItIs: At an incident, warn traffic, call 999 and be ready to give first aid. If your lorry is in a collision that causes damage or injury, you must stop and give your details.

keyFacts.text: Collision causing damage or injury: you MUST stop and give your details to anyone with reasonable grounds to ask.
Details not given at the time? You MUST report it to the police as soon as reasonably practicable, within 24 hours.
Injury, and no insurance certificate shown at the time: you MUST produce it to the police within seven days.

keyFacts: Don't move injured people from their vehicles unless they are in immediate danger.
Burns: cool for at least 20 minutes with plenty of clean, cool water.

visual.caption: First aid at the scene: D R A B C (Highway Code annex 7)

rows: Check it is safe to approach. Switch off engines and stop anyone smoking.
Gently shake their shoulders and ask loudly 'Are you all right?'
No response? Lift the chin forward with your fingers to open the airway.
No signs of breathing? Start CPR: press hard and fast, 5 to 6 cm, about twice a second.
Check for bleeding. Apply firm pressure over the wound (not on anything stuck in it).

a.label: Within 24 hours
points: Report the collision to the police
If you didn't give your details at the scene

b.label: Within seven days
points: Produce your insurance certificate to the police
After an injury collision where you did not show it

onTheTest.question: You're first at a crash. A casualty is not responding and not breathing. What should you do?
options: Give them a drink of water
Pull them out of the vehicle
onTheTest.why: If there are no signs of breathing, start CPR. Keep going until they breathe or a medical professional takes over.

onTheTest.question: Your lorry damages a parked car and you can't find the owner. What must you do?
options: Report it to the police within 24 hours
Leave a note and drive on
onTheTest.why: If you don't give your details at the time, report it to the police as soon as reasonably practicable, and in any case within 24 hours.

traps: 24 hours is for reporting to the police; seven days is for producing your insurance.
Don't give casualties anything to eat or drink.
Don't remove a motorcyclist's helmet unless it is essential.

sources.ref: Annex 7: First aid on the road

review.checkedAgainst: Highway Code rules 283, 286, 287 (RTA 1988 s170); annex 7 first aid on the road (sections 1 to 4, burns)
